==English==
{{wp|+ (surname)}}

===Etymology===
Various origins:
* [[English]] metonymic occupational surname for a cobbler, from {{m|en|last|t=a tool for shaping shoes|id=tool}}. Compare {{m|en|Laster}}.
* Also as an English surname, from the adjective {{m|en|last}}.
* Borrowed from {{bor|en|nl|-}} and {{bor|en|de|Last}}, an occupational surname for a porter (see the German entry below).

===Proper noun===
{{en-proper noun|s}}

# {{surname|en}}.

====Statistics====
* According to the 2010 United States Census, ''Last'' is the 15922<sup>nd</sup> most common surname in the United States, belonging to 1825 individuals. ''Last'' is most common among White (92.66%) individuals.

===Further reading===
* {{R:en:DAFN}}

{{wp|Medes}}
{{swp|+#Places}}

===Etymology===
{{bor+|en|la|Mēdia}}, from {{der|en|grc|Μηδία}}, from {{m|grc|Μῆδος}}, from {{m|xme-old||*Mada}} (vocalization uncertain), the {{der|en|xme-old|-}} language self-designator signifying speakers of the Median language. Compare {{cog|peo|𐎶𐎠𐎭|tr=Māda}}. Ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*médʰyos||middle}} i.e. central kingdom, cognate with {{cog|sa|sc=Deva|मध्य|tr=mádhya}}.

==English==

===Etymology===
* As an English surname, from the adjective {{m|en|new}}.
* Also as an English surname, from a misdivision of {{der|en|enm|atten}} {{m|enm|ew|t=at the yew}}.
* As a {{der|en|de|-}} and Jewish surname, Americanized from {{m|en|Neu}}.
* As a {{der|en|zh|-}} surname, from a Romanization of {{m|zh|牛}} (see {{m|en|Niu}}) and {{m|zh|梁}} (see {{m|en|Liang}}).
